note: Shows choosing melodies by filter: each melody-singer names a difficulty and a stage with pick instead of a tune number, the second a step harder than the first. The why says what makes a step tune easier than a skip, the step tune comes back in A from the Key row, and the text says what Play starts (the tune and the mic) and what to sing on.

exercise.title: Two tunes: steps, then skips
exercise.focus: An easy Do Re Mi tune in G and A, then a medium Do Mi Sol tune in D
exercise.why: In a tune that moves by step each note sits right next to the last one, while a skip asks you to hear the next note before you jump to it, so the step tune comes first.

sections.text: A tune on Do, Re and Mi. Press Play below to hear it: the mic starts with it, and your pitch shows on the staff. Sing along on the note names, which help you remember each sound. Once it feels easy, tap A in the Key row above the staff and sing it there. The notes change, the pattern doesn't.
A longer tune in D that skips between Do, Mi and Sol, then steps back down. Look at the staff first and guess how it goes. Press Play below to check your guess, then sing along on "la".
